I am writing as a long-time Call of Duty fan to express serious concerns about the current state of older Call of Duty titles on PC, particularly those available on Steam.

When it comes to the Call of Duty series, the first thing that most players think of is definitely Modern Warfare, which makes Black Ops the most underrated in the Call of Duty series in terms of plot. Unlike the grand scenes and grand plots of Modern Warfare, Black Ops was probably the first famous shooter game to dare to take the Cold War as its theme, and at the same time, the depth of its plot is extraordinary, creating an unparalleled sense of suspense and atmosphere that is no less than that of the Modern Warfare series.

The game's plot is actually quite remarkable, both in 2010 and compared to other Call of Duty predecessors, an unprecedented attempt that players who love the Call of Duty series but have never tried it before should not miss. In addition, the game's zombie mode is also both highly playable and interesting, and the multiplayer mode is also quite well designed.
 
However, in terms of graphics, Call of Duty: Black Ops is slightly inferior to the 2009 release of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, and there are often a variety of bugs that seriously ruins the game experience on the way to play. The game's obscure plot is a boon to players who like to dig deeper into the game's story development, but this different attempt with the previous Call of Duty series is often not in line with the taste of players seeking an easy and exciting game experience.

I believe that the vast majority of players have long tried Black Ops, more for nostalgia and come. If you are for the call of duty series of single-player campaigns and have not tried black ops, please remember to give it a try, black ops will not let you down. It is worth mentioning that even now, the multiplayer mode still has a certain number of players. Due to the presence of Call of Duty: World at War characters, it is recommended to play the game after completing the Call of Duty: World at War storyline.

Title: WARNING: Critical Security Vulnerabilities (RAT Exploits)

I strongly advise against purchasing or playing this game. The game has long been plagued by serious security vulnerabilities that allow attackers to gain remote access to players’ computers via so-called RCE (Remote Code Execution) exploits (RAT – Remote Access Trojan).

These security risks have been known for years but have never been satisfactorily addressed in many of the older Call of Duty titles (from BO1 to BO3). Anyone who launches the game nonetheless is exposing their entire PC and personal data to unnecessary risk.

It is unacceptable for a publisher like Activision to leave its players in such insecure environments. As long as these exploits have not been officially and permanently patched, installing this game poses a massive security risk.

Please research the topic “CoD RCE exploit” yourself before launching the game. I have permanently uninstalled the game due to these security concerns.

A classic CoD. One of the best in the series.

Pros: 
Great campaign. Tells the story of a brainwashed CIA agent who lost his memory and is being interrogated to find the location of where the main antagonist is located. Missions take places around the globe in locations such as US, Cuba, Russia, and Vietnam.
Fun multiplayer. One of the best multiplayers in the CoD franchise. Great maps, great weapons, and fun killstreaks. This game is the first CoD to have iconic maps like Nuketown or Firing Range. The combat training mode is fun too. It's a fun mode where you can rank up playing with bots. (Wish CoD would bring that feature back) The multiplayer also had dedicated servers unlike the console versions.
Zombies: My personal favorite zombies of all the CoDs. I love the classic maps Kino Der Toten and Five.
Good graphics. (For its time)

Cons:
A bit pricey for a 10+ year old game.
DLC is not free and still costs full price.
May not run well on low end PCs.
You sometimes run into hackers in multiplayer.
Last Stand perk.

All in all, this game is a solid game. I would recommend it if you want a good/classic CoD experience. Imo this game is worth playing for the campaign and zombies alone. But I don't recommend buying the game at this price. Wait for a sale.

I have 2k hours logged onto steam for this game, but the real number is somewhere around 4-5k because I spent more than half my time playing in offline mode (mainly to prevent steam weekly updates from crashing or closing my games during long pauses). I could care less about the game's multiplayer, and this review will only take Zombies and Campaign into account (I speedrun the two modes). The Zombies mode in this game is the strongest out of any CoD Zombies game, period. It has the perfect amount of challenge and difficult to master movement and gameplay mechanics. The campaign's story is probably one of the better known ones in the CoD franchise, but I would not buy it solely for that purpose considering that a casual playthrough will take 5 - 7 hours at most. I think if you like the traditional CoD zombies mode, you'll find great enjoyment sinking hours and hours into this game, mastering each of the maps and constantly improving your best rounds on them. The gunplay in this game still feels better than most modern CoDs with their weird recoil patterns and hard-to-see-through scopes. The lack of visual clutter combined with the minimalistic screen effects and UI is also refreshing to see every time I revisit this game. My only big issue is that Activision continues to list the game at a price tag of 40$ USD, which is totally unacceptable for a game that is more than 11 years old at the time that this review goes up.

But here's the actual review of the game,
It's a fantastic game, gameplay does feel a bit old, but that doesn't stop it from being fun.
The campaign is easily one of the best campaigns in any call of duty, and everyone should play it.
Mason's story is very interesting, but I won't say much because I don't want to spoil anything.

The Zombies mode Is absolutely amazing, as always, it's way better with friends, but that won't stop you from having fun in solo. The base game includes 2 zombies maps, those are "Kino der toten" and "FIVE". 

Kino is a simplistic  map, taking place in an abandoned theatre, getting to the upgrade machine is simple and it's a good launch map, for newcomers who need to learn the basics. Despite this, it's still a fun map to play even if you are a zombies master.

FIVE, takes place in the pentagon, and is tied with the campaigns story, once you've think you've gotten the hang of zombies in kino, you should try FIVE. This map is much more difficult. There are 3 main floors, all of which are difficult to survive in, getting to the upgrade machine is more challenging than in kino, and there aren't too many good wall guns to buy. This map is best played with 3 or 4 players. It's an underrated map, and has much more to offer than Kino.

Zombies quick play multiplayer with random people, is still somewhat active. You can get into a game of kino with 4 other players quite easily, may take slightly longer with FIVE but there are plenty of people playing.
The dlc maps are a different story, you'll be lucky to find 1 person, let alone 3. Good luck trying to get into a game of der riese with randoms.

The multiplayer of Black ops 1 is still extremely active, with lots of players. It is an extremely fun mode, with some extreme levels of grind, but its still always fun. Lots of things to unlock, you can play with friends, theres just so much to do in this mode i cant even begin to describe it all.
Easily the one of, if not the best call of duty multiplayer mode ever.

Call of Duty Black Ops is a game with an atmosphere so dense that it hits you the moment you look at the cover art. Seeing this game at GameStop with that mysterious figure holding two M1911s engraved with the names Mustang and Sally was enough to get me on my hands and knees begging for a copy, just so I could be part of the cool kids playing rated M games. Before you even press start it already feels different. That main menu alone is still unmatched and easily the best of all time. The music, the interrogation chair, the unease. It immediately locks you in and tells you this is not just another military shooter.

The campaign is where Black Ops truly separates itself. It leans hard into psychological thriller, political paranoia, and Cold War espionage in a way the series has never quite replicated since. It is cinematic without feeling shallow and constantly keeps you questioning what is real and what is manipulation. The characters are iconic, elevated even further by an absurdly stacked cast. Gary Oldman as Viktor Reznov is still insane to think about, especially because there is not a shred of Gary Oldman visible in the performance. It took me years to even realize it was him. Sam Worthington as Alex Mason is burned into my brain so deeply that whenever I see him in other films I only hear Mason. These performances feel career defining and give the story a weight that most shooters never even attempt. Jump to the current day and Call of Duty has released games with campaigns that are either completely missing or painfully phoned in, which makes Black Ops feel even more special in retrospect.

Multiplayer was equally transformative. Black Ops introduced a level of customization and progression that fundamentally changed Call of Duty forever. Creating your own loadouts, managing currency, and experimenting with playstyles felt fresh and endlessly replayable. So many approaches were viable that entire communities formed around them. The competitive scene, pubstomping, sniping, trickshotting. It was competitive but also playful, the kind of multiplayer that encouraged experimentation and long nights with friends rather than pure optimization.

And then there is Zombies. An all time classic mode that holds some of my favorite memories in gaming, and honestly some of my favorite memories in life. Late nights, split screen, learning maps, chasing Easter eggs, arguing over doors and perks. What truly elevates Zombies to legendary status is its soundtrack. Songs like 115 are among the best tracks ever associated with a video game. That industrial metal sound did something to my brain at a formative age and is a core reason I am a metalhead to this day. Hitting a flow state deep into a Zombies match, blasting 115 while listening to the orgasmic pew pew pew of Pack a Punched weapons, is an experience that still sinks its teeth into me. It is the kind of thing that makes me ruin my sleep schedule even now as an adult because once you are locked in, it is impossible to walk away. This soundtrack is a headbanger that fuels me in the gym and more importantly fuels me while taking out hordes of zombies.

This was a blockbuster video game in the truest sense of the word. Campaign, multiplayer, zombies, and even the extra modes felt thoughtfully crafted and packed with passion. It feels like a game overflowing with secrets, as if the developers cared about players poking around and discovering more than what was immediately in front of them.

That said, the version on Steam is a real shame. Mods are basically required to get the best experience, whether that is increasing FOV or finding functional multiplayer servers. The fact that it often still sells at full price while requiring community fixes would normally earn a negative review from me. But the core of Black Ops is so strong, so influential, and so far above its peers that I cannot in good faith give it anything but praise. I think it’s a greater value than any of the last three Call of Duty’s released combined. 

If there is one thing I wish Activision would seriously consider, it is something similar to The Master Chief Collection but for Call of Duty. I understand there are probably massive technical hurdles with so many games running on different engines, but a unified collection that preserves and modernizes these classics feels like a no brainer. Something like that could absolutely bring back fans that the newer titles have lost, myself included. There is clearly still hunger for this era of Call of Duty, and Black Ops is one of the strongest arguments for why it deserves to be preserved properly.

Black Ops is pivotal to my taste as an adult. The Call of Duty games from this era were packed with hundreds of hours of fun and shared memories, something that feels completely unrecognizable compared to the current state of the franchise. This game is lightning in a bottle, a defining moment not just for Call of Duty but for mainstream gaming as a whole. I seriously cannot scream its praises enough into this review. This was purely a moment in the industry. 

If I had one wish it would be to go back to being a kid again, staying up late in secret from my parents, chasing levels and chasing high rounds. Even if it was just for one night. These are times I will never get back, but times I never would have had if it was not for this game. I wish I could recreate them with a group, but the hardest pill to swallow is that the world has moved on.
